content.intro: Security begins at trust boundaries. Validate data for the intended operation, encode output for its exact context, constrain file and network access, protect credentials, and apply authorization consistently. In this lesson, focus on how injection occurs; then compare it with parameterized statements. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use sql injection when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Security begins at trust boundaries. Validate data for the intended operation, encode output for its exact context, constrain file and network access, protect credentials, and apply authorization consistently. For sql injection, begin with how injection occurs. Also distinguish parameterized statements; avoiding dynamic sql concatenation; allowlisting identifiers when dynamic identifiers are necessary. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

items.title: How injection occurs
items.text: Treat the relevant value as untrusted, apply the defense at the correct boundary, and verify a deliberately invalid or hostile-looking input is rejected or encoded.

items.title: Parameterized statements
items.text: Know when to use parameterized statements, what input or program state it changes, and which boundary case is worth testing.

items.title: Avoiding dynamic SQL concatenation
items.text: Keep query structure separate from data values, check failures explicitly, and use constraints or transactions when integrity depends on multiple operations.

content_blocks.title: A small PHP example for SQL Injection
content_blocks.code:

$sql = "SELECT id, name FROM products WHERE category = :category";
$params = [":category" => "books"];
echo str_contains($sql, ":category") && isset($params[":category"]) ? "named placeholder ready" : "check binding";

content_blocks.title: Professional habit
content_blocks.text: Validate data at system boundaries and encode output for the target context; validation and escaping solve different problems.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating input validation as output escaping.
common_mistakes.why: A value can be valid data and still be unsafe in an HTML or JavaScript output context.
common_mistakes.fix: Validate shape and business rules at input boundaries, then apply context-appropriate output encoding.

common_mistakes.why: A request can be sent without the original form or browser UI.
common_mistakes.fix: Repeat all security-relevant validation and authorization on the server.

common_mistakes.problem: Returning internal error details to the browser.
common_mistakes.why: Stack traces and configuration values may expose sensitive information.
common_mistakes.fix: Log safe diagnostics server-side and return a generic, useful response.
